messages:
Alex S.: Quick sync — ACME wants a committed plan for a POC->prod ramp. They expect ~500 QPS combined (chat gen ~350 QPS, embeddings/rerank ~150 QPS) during 09:00–18:00 PST. Security questionnaire due EOD Friday. Need recommended reserved GPU count, autoscale policy (min/max), and an estimate for monthly reservation pricing + burst behavior. Anyone?
Mira (SE): Can you share the traffic profile (avg tokens per request / tail percentiles) and model choice? 500 QPS can mean very different capacity depending on tokens and model.
Alex S.: Good call — initial profile: chat avg 64 tokens in, 128 tokens out. Embeds are short (<=64 tokens). 95th p50 latency target ~250ms for chat. They want to use our quantized 8B variant we proposed.
Sam-ML: With quantized 8B and our current kernels, rough ballpark is: 1 GPU ≈ 40–70 chat QPS at 128 out tokens depending on batching and KV cache warm. Embeds are cheap — you can get ~300–500 embed QPS per GPU. So for mixed traffic I'd partition load: reserve for chat throughput primarily.
Sam-ML: Quick calc: to cover 350 chat QPS at 60 QPS/GPU we'd reserve 6 GPUs (6*60=360). For embeds, those can run on same pool but effectively add ~1 GPU worth of headroom. So reserve 7 GPUs minimum, set autoscale max to 12 for bursts.
Mira (SE): +1 to Sam's calc. Also recommend a preheat window before business hours to populate KV cache and prefix cache. For p95 latency we should instruct ops to pre-warm ~30–45 minutes.
Jordan (SRE): Autoscale details — set min_replicas to 6, max_replicas to 12, scale_step 1, cooldown 120s, target_qps_per_replica 55. Use queued requests limit per-replica to protect p95. Example policy:
```json
{
  "min_replicas": 6,
  "max_replicas": 12,
  "target_qps_per_replica": 55,
  "scale_cooldown_seconds": 120,
  "preheat_schedule": "09:00-09:30 PST"
}
```
Alex S.: That helps. What's the pricing delta for reserving 7 vs 4 GPUs? They asked about a smaller commit with burst credits.
Mira (SE): Reserved pricing is tiered; ballpark: 7 reserved GPUs -> ~0.48x on-host spot/usage vs on-demand. If they want a smaller commit we can do 4 reserved + burst to 12. Burst uses pooled capacity and is best-effort; SLA only covers reserved. I'd flag that to them.
Tia-Sec: Security questionnaire note — we need to confirm KMS integration for customer-managed keys, VPC peering option, and logs retention. There was a question about on-disk encryption for caches; answer: KV caches are memory-first but persisted shards are encrypted with our vault keys by default. I'll fill the exact field in the questionnaire.
Alex S.: Perfect — can you paste the exact wording for the questionnaire fields so I can send to their security contact?
Tia-Sec: Paste for KMS: "We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; keys are limited to control-plane operations and encryption at rest for persisted cache shards." For VPC: "Private deployment via VPC peering and IP allowlist supported; control plane remains in Redwood unless Private deployment requested."
Mira (SE): For cost modeling I'm attaching our quick estimator (internal link): https://redwood.internal/sales/estimators/acme-poc. Use conservative throughput (60 QPS/GPU) and include preheat hours.
Alex S.: Any known enterprise blockers for committing to 7 GPUs? Legal or procurement usually asks for a minimum commit term. CTO also asked about failover if we lose a zone.
Jordan (SRE): For AZ failover: recommend cross-AZ placement and autoscale policy that spins up healthy replicas in other AZs. If they need guaranteed cross-AZ capacity, we should add +1 GPU as runway. Also call out regional fallback — we can route to another region under policy but that changes latency.
Sam-ML: Operational note: if traffic is very spiky, consider model sharding + split routing (serve embeddings on CPU-backed pod pool if acceptable) to reduce GPU footprint. That changes cost math but is an ops tradeoff.
Alex S.: Action items: (1) Mira — send the 7GPU vs 4GPU+burst cost comparison and estimator link to ACME. (2) Tia — paste finalized questionnaire answers in the doc and send to Alex. (3) Jordan/SRE — confirm preheat runbook and sample autoscale policy that we can include in SOW.
Mira (SE): Will do, sending a short one-pager and cost table in 30m. :thumbsup:
Tia-Sec: I'll update questionnaire now and share in the thread.
Jordan (SRE): I'll drop the preheat/playbook snippet and sample runbook items here by EOD.
deploy-bot: scheduled preheat job created: job_id=preheat-acme-2769876543 scheduled_at=2026-04-02T08:30:00-07:00
Alex S.: Thanks team — I'll coordinate with ACME CISO and procurement. If they push back on minimum commit we'll propose 4 reserved + burst credits + cross-AZ add-on.
Mira (SE): FYI — if they want a lower latency p95 target we should recommend +1 GPU to the reserved baseline (so 8 reserved).
Alex S.: Noted. Closing loop after the call at 11:00.
